title: Align Glob tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all Glob improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go Glob is close on the basic pattern/path surface and now uses ripgrep/doublestar-backed discovery, but it is not fully aligned with the TS reference in permission lifecycle wiring, file-read/plugin ignore integration, structured output shape and exact result text, cwd/session scoping, native/fallback sorting plus truncation order, strict schema/tool metadata, and timeout/buffer partial-result robustness. Existing Go tests cover many local helpers, but the Glob test baseline is stale in places and the current focused go test command is blocked before Glob execution by an unrelated compile error in prompt/context.go:82.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Tool-level read permission and allowed-directory wiring are incomplete for Glob
improvement_points.description: The TS Glob tool participates in the central permission lifecycle: it exposes getPath, validates the path, prepares permission matchers from the pattern, and delegates to checkReadPermissionForTool. The Go Glob tool is a stateless Execute-only tool; allowed search directory helpers exist, but SetupRegistry and UpdateSessionContext do not wire allowedDirs into search tools, and the generic Tool interface has no permission hook equivalent. In default runtime wiring, Glob can therefore search any os.Getwd-relative path unless tests manually set package globals.

improvement_points.title: File-read deny rules and orphaned plugin-cache exclusions are not wired like TS
improvement_points.description: TS derives read-deny ignore patterns from the live tool permission context for every Glob invocation, normalizes them to the current searchDir, and adds them to ripgrep as negative --glob filters before results are collected. TS also computes session-scoped orphaned plugin-cache exclusions and adds them before running ripgrep. Go has filtering helpers and setters, but the setters are only used by tests in the searched code, and the main ripgrep path filters after collecting all results instead of passing exclusions into ripgrep.

improvement_points.title: Structured output data and exact tool_result text do not match TS
improvement_points.description: TS Glob has an explicit output schema with durationMs, numFiles, filenames, and truncated, and call() returns that object as data. The mapper then emits exact model-facing text: 'No files found' for empty results, or filenames plus a fixed truncation sentence. Go returns a plain ToolResult.Content string plus string Metadata keys with different names, and its empty/truncation text differs from TS.

improvement_points.title: Native/fallback paths do not sort the full candidate set before truncation
improvement_points.description: TS relies on ripgrep --sort=modified, converts all returned paths to absolute paths, then applies offset/limit slicing. Go's normal ripgrep path mostly follows this, but the doublestar native path walks in filesystem order, filters, and truncates before Execute sorts the already-capped display paths. The explicit fallback path sorts newest-first and truncates before the final Execute sort. This changes which 100 files are returned when the native/fallback path has more than defaultGlobLimit matches.

improvement_points.title: CWD scoping is process-global in Go but async-context-scoped in TS
improvement_points.description: TS getCwd is backed by AsyncLocalStorage and AgentTool wraps worktree/explicit-cwd execution with runWithCwdOverride, so Glob's default path and output relativization follow the current agent context. Go Glob resolves the default search root and display paths with os.Getwd. SetupRegistry has RuntimeScope and UpdateSessionContext, but GlobTool receives neither, so concurrent agent/worktree execution cannot provide a per-invocation cwd without changing the whole process directory.

improvement_points.title: Strict input validation and TS tool metadata are not represented
improvement_points.description: TS uses z.strictObject for Glob input and exposes searchHint, maxResultSizeChars, read-only, concurrency-safe, auto-classifier input, and search/read classification. Go's schema has matching top-level parameter names but no strict additional-properties behavior, parseInputOrError ignores unknown JSON fields, and the Tool interface/Glob implementation do not expose read-only/concurrency/search classifier metadata. registry/tool_visibility.go also does not provide a Glob searchHint fallback.

improvement_points.title: Glob does not align ripgrep timeout and buffer-overflow partial-result behavior
improvement_points.description: TS ripGrep returns partial lines when timeout or buffer overflow produced output, and only rejects no-output timeouts with a descriptive RipgrepTimeoutError. Go runRipgrep captures partial output in RipgrepTimeoutError, but GlobTool.Execute treats every returned error as a plain error response, discarding partials. Go's cappedBuffer also records dropped output, but runRipgrep and Glob do not propagate that as a truncation/partial condition.

improvement_points.title: Go Glob tests are stale/conflicting and current package verification is blocked
improvement_points.description: The current test files contain stale comments claiming now-passing behavior must fail, and two Glob mtime tests assert opposite directions. The intended TS behavior is the source-level ripgrep --sort=modified plus post-ripgrep slicing path, so the Go tests need a single TS-replay expectation, plus coverage for native/fallback over-limit selection, permission wiring through SetupRegistry, structured output, and partial timeout behavior. A focused go test command for Glob currently fails before running tests because prompt/context.go refers to types.Message.IsMeta, which is absent from the current types.Message.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire Glob into read-permission and allowed-directory lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: SetupRegistry and UpdateSessionContext configure search allowed directories for Glob/Grep from the same allowedDirs passed to file tools.
Glob rejects or permission-denies path roots outside allowedDirs in production registry wiring, not only when tests manually call SetAllowedSearchDirs.
Absolute-pattern base directories are checked against the same allowed root policy before ripgrep/native matching runs.
Tests cover allowed and denied roots via SetupRegistry or the runtime setup path.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire file-read deny rules and plugin-cache exclusions into Glob searches
dependencies: GLOB-TASK-001 if permission context/allowed root plumbing is needed as the source of read deny rules
acceptance_criteria: Runtime setup populates file-read deny patterns from settings/permission context rather than relying on tests calling SetFileReadIgnorePatterns.
Runtime setup populates orphaned plugin-cache exclusions or an equivalent lazy/frozen session cache.
Ripgrep receives deny/plugin exclusions as negative --glob args before result collection where possible; post-filtering remains only as defense-in-depth.
Denied and orphaned paths do not consume the first 100 user-visible result slots.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align Glob structured output and exact model-facing result text
acceptance_criteria: Glob exposes TS-equivalent fields: filenames, durationMs, numFiles, and truncated, with TS names and types available to downstream consumers.
Empty result model text is exactly 'No files found'.
Truncation suffix is exactly '(Results are truncated. Consider using a more specific path or pattern.)'.
Metadata, if retained for Go internals, does not replace or rename the TS output contract.

implementation_subtasks.title: Normalize Glob ordering and limit selection across ripgrep, doublestar, and fallback
acceptance_criteria: All Glob execution paths sort the full candidate set according to the TS reference before applying defaultGlobLimit.
The doublestar/native path for bracket patterns returns the same first 100 files as a TS/ripgrep reference fixture.
The rg-unavailable fallback path uses the same ordering direction and truncation point as TS reference behavior.
Conflicting mtime tests are replaced with one TS-backed expectation.

implementation_subtasks.title: Give Glob per-session/per-agent cwd state instead of os.Getwd-only behavior
acceptance_criteria: GlobTool can resolve omitted path and display-relative paths from an injected runtime scope/current cwd.
UpdateSessionContext updates Glob/Grep cwd state along with Bash, PowerShell, and RuntimeScope.
Concurrent or nested agent/worktree tests prove one agent's Glob default cwd does not depend on process-global os.Chdir.
formatSearchDisplayPath no longer uses os.Getwd for Glob/Grep paths when a scoped cwd is available.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align Glob input strictness and tool metadata
acceptance_criteria: Glob input rejects unknown fields or the Go schema/runtime provides the equivalent of TS z.strictObject.
Glob exposes read-only, concurrency-safe, search/read classification, auto-classifier input, max result size, and searchHint metadata through Go's tool metadata mechanism.
ToolSearch/discovery can rank Glob using the TS searchHint equivalent when relevant.
Tests cover unknown-field rejection and metadata discovery for Glob.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align Glob timeout, partial-result, and stdout-cap behavior with TS ripGrep
acceptance_criteria: When ripgrep times out after producing complete lines, Glob returns those partial lines instead of a hard error, matching TS ripGrep behavior.
When ripgrep times out with no output, Glob surfaces a clear timeout error rather than 'no files found'.
When stdout is capped/dropped, Glob drops incomplete trailing output and surfaces truncation/partial metadata instead of silently returning a clipped line.
Tests use a fake rg or controllable helper to cover timeout with output, timeout without output, and capped stdout.

implementation_subtasks.title: Clean and extend the Glob parity test baseline
dependencies: Fix the unrelated prompt/context.go:82 build blocker before package-level verification can run
acceptance_criteria: Stale 'must fail' comments are removed or rewritten as current parity assertions.
Mtime expectations are unified against the TS reference behavior.

risks: Some subtasks touch shared runtime surfaces; coordinate with foundation tasks to avoid incompatible local adapters.
non_goals: Do not make unrelated behavior changes outside this tool unless required by a listed dependency.
notes_for_assignee: Start by adding or updating parity fixtures, then implement the smallest vertical slice that makes a failing fixture pass. Keep TS evidence lines in comments or test names where useful.
